<entry id="S00804">
<head-word>קָטַע</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (cmp. גָּדַע) 
<italic>to cut off, lop, mutilate</italic>.</definition>
<notes> B. Kam. VIII, 1. Ib. 7 האומר … קְטַע את ידי וכ' if one says to one’s neighbor, cut my hand off, he (who did so) is bound to pay damages. Ab. Zar. I, 5 קוֹטֵעַ את וכ' one may cut off its toe and sell the cock to the idolater. Ib. 10
<sup>b</sup> יִקְטְעֶנָּה, v. נוֹמִי; a. fr.—Part. pass. קָטוּעַ. Nidd. 64
<sup>b</sup>; Keth. 10
<sup>b</sup> דור ק', v. דּוֹרְקְטִי.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pi.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>קִיטֵּעַ</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> same, also 
<italic>to cut through</italic>.</definition>
<notes> B. Kam. 83
<sup>b</sup> יכול … מְקַטֵּעַ את ידו (Ms. M. נְקַטֵּעַ) (from Ex. XXI, 24) you might think, if a person cut a man’s hand off, one (we, the court) should cut his hand off. Tanḥ. Ḥayé 3 מְקַטְּעִין ויוצאין וכ' they (the waters) cut through and come forth between the mountains.—
<italic>Part. pass</italic>. מְקוּטָּע; f. מְקוּטַּעַת; 
<italic>pl</italic>. מְקוּטָּעִים, מְקוּטָּעִין; מְקוּטָּעוֹת 
<italic>lopped, defective</italic>. Pesik. R. s. 31 שהיו אצבעותיהם מק' their fingers were mutilated (bitten off).—חדשים מק' (or sub. חדשים) incomplete months, a fraction of the last month of pregnancy. Y. Bets. I, beg. 60
<sup>a</sup>, v. סוּם I. Bekh. 21
<sup>a</sup> אינה יולדת למק' an animal does not give birth before the due number of months is completed; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִתְקַטֵּעַ, </binyan-form>
<binyan-name>Nithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִתְקַטֵּעַ</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to be cut off, crippled</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Pesik. R. l. c. ונִתְקַטְּעוּ אצבעותינו our fingers were mutilated (by the handcuffs); Midr. Till. to Ps. CXXXVII; Yalk. Ps. 884. Taan. 21
<sup>a</sup> רגלי … יִתְקַטְּעוּ may my feet that paid no regard to thy feet be crippled.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="S00805">
<head-word>קְטַע</head-word>
<language-key> ch. </language-key>
<language-reference>same</language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>, </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to cut off, break off</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. II Chr. XXXIV, 4 (h. text גדע). Targ. Y. Deut. XIX, 5. Targ. Y. II Num. XIII, 23. Targ. Y. Ex. XXXIX, 3; a. fr.—Lam. R. to I, 1 (העיר) קְטַע קִטְעָךְ cut thy cut (garment, i.e. mind thy own business). Y. Sabb. VI, 8
<sup>c</sup> bot. מִיקְטוֹעַ, v. כֵּיסָא. Y. Meg. IV, 75
<sup>b</sup> bot., v. דִּיבּוּרָא. Ib. אין קַטְעוּן רישך וכ' and if they were to cut thy head off, do not listen to them; a. fr.—Part. pass. קְטִיעַ; f. קְטִיעָא; 
<plural-form>pl. קְטִיעִין; קְטִיעָן</plural-form>. Targ. Y. Num. XI, 32 דק' he that was crippled. Targ. Y. Ex. XXI, 21 תרין יומין ק' two days incomplete (v. preced.). Targ. Y. Gen. XLVI, 29; a. e.—Pesik. Naḥămu, p. 125
<sup>b</sup>, a. e.—ק' לישנא tongue-cut, stammerer, v. פְּסִילּוֹסָא.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to cut short, end</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 44; Yalk. ib. 77, v. מִלְכָי.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to form cakes</italic> (v. 
<xref rid="S00810">קְטַף</xref>).</definition>
<notes> Targ. Y. Ex. XII, 39.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>קַטַּע</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> same.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Job XVI, 13 Ms. (ed. 
<italic>Pe.</italic>; h. text יפלח). Targ. II Chr. II, 9; a. e.—Y. Sabb. VII, 10
<sup>a</sup> bot.; Y. Bets. IV, 62
<sup>c</sup> bot., v. בגומא. Y. Meg. l. c. ולינן מְקַטְּעִין לון וכ' do we not break a portion of the Pentateuch (סִדְרָא) for their sake (divide the recitation of a Sidra among the school children)? Y. Ned. IX, 41
<sup>c</sup> (we say to him who vowed revenge, ref. to Lev. XIX, 18) הוה מְקַטָּע … תחזור ותמחי לידיה he chopped meat, and the knife struck his hand, wilt thou again strike his hand?, i.e. if he did wrong, he hurt himself. Y. Sabb. XII, beg. 13
<sup>c</sup>, v. פְּסִיפָּס. Bets. 25
<sup>b</sup> מקטע רגליהון וכ', v. חֲצוּבָא II, a. נְטִיעָה.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Ithpe.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>אִתְקְטַע</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to be cut, shortened</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Y. Gen. XXIV, 61. Targ. Koh. VIII, 13.—Y. Peah VIII, end, 21
<sup>b</sup> ידיה … יִתְקַטְעוּן, v. פְּשַׁט.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="S00810">
<head-word>קָטַף</head-word>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="S00804"> cmp. קטע</xref>,
<xref rid="S00774"> קטל</xref>,
<xref rid="A00083"> a. גדף)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to cut, break off, pluck</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Lam. R. to I, 12, v. עוֹלֵלָה.—Part. pass. קָטוּף; f. קְטוּפָה. Ber. 47
<sup>a</sup>; Tosef. Meg. IV (III), 27, a. e. אמן ק', v. infra.—Pirké d’R. El. ch. XXIX עוללות קְטוּפִין premature (undeveloped) grapes.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Nif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִקְטָף, </binyan-form>
<binyan-name>Hithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִתְקטֵּף</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to be plucked, broken off</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Tosef. l. c. העונה אמן … קטופה יִקָּטְפוּ שנותיו he who pronounces a broken Amen (v. אָמֵן II), his years shall be broken off; Ber. l. c. יִתְקַטְּפוּ; Y. ib. VIII, end, 12
<sup>c</sup> תִּקָּטֵף נשמתו his soul shall be plucked off (he shall die before his time).</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pi.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>קִיטֵּף</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition> same. Esth. R. to I, 9, v. same.</definition>
<notes> Esth. R. to I, 9, v. עוֹלֵלָה.—Esp. ק' בעוללות [
<italic>to do plucking among the small single bunches</italic>,] 
<italic>to initiate persecution with attempts to destroy the young generation</italic>. Gen. R. s. 42 הראשון התחיל מְקַטֵּף בע' וכ' the first enemy began with breaking off the young bunches, the second with thinning the clusters (v. וִּנֵּב) &c.; Lev. R. s. 11; Ruth R. introd. (ושם האיש).—Nidd. 66
<sup>b</sup> בנתר משום דמקטף she must not wash her head with natron, because it plucks (uproots) the weakly rooted hairs (which left on the head prevent the water from immediate contact with the body; v. חוּץ I); a. fr.—Trnsf. (of fire) 
<italic>to creep along the ground of a field</italic>, opp. קָדַח. Y. B. Kam. VI, 5
<sup>c</sup> top במְקַטֶּפֶת (Bab. ib. 61
<sup>a</sup> בנכפפת), v. קָדַח.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to tear in pieces a lump of dough</italic> to form cakes, for which purpose the kneader moistens his hands with water, oil &c.; hence: 
<italic>to form dough and smoothen its surface</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Pes. II, end, 29
<sup>c</sup> אין לשין … אבל מְקַטְּפִין וכ' you must not knead unleavened bread (for the Passover night) with liquors (juice of fruit, oil &c.) but you may form it with liquors; Bab. ib. 36
<sup>a</sup>. Ib. את שלשין בו מקטפין בו only such liquid as may be used for kneading, should be used for forming. Ib. 42
<sup>a</sup> אחד שמְקַטֶּפֶת וכ' one vessel in which she dips her hand when forming the cakes, and another &c.; a. e.—
<italic>Part. pass.</italic> מְקוּטָּף; f. מְקוּטֶּפֶת &c. 
<italic>broken off, nipped</italic> Midr. Till. to Ps. LXXIII, 4 האשה … אחת מק' ואחת מעוכה ed. Bub. (ed. מעוסה, corr. acc.) when a woman spins a yarn, once a thread is broken (and must be knotted), and once it is rubbed off (crumbled, too thin). Gen. R. s. 99 
<pgbrk id="pg1352" />יצא … ואזניו מק' Reuben came forth with his ears clipped (his pride humbled); (comment.: his ears hanging down like a nipped plant, i.e. saddened).</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="S00811">
<head-word>קְטַף</head-word>
<hw-number>I</hw-number>
<language-key> ch. </language-key>
<language-reference>same.</language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition />
<notes> Targ. O. Lev. XXV, 11 (Y. 
<italic>Pa.</italic>; h. text בצר). Targ. Deut. XXIII, 26. Targ. I Sam. II, 31 (h. text גדע). Targ. Ez. V, 11 (h. text !גרע); a. fr.—Lam. R. to I, 22 קַטֵּיף … דקְטַפְתְּ וכ', v. עוֹלְלָא. Y. Gitt. III, end, 45
<sup>b</sup> דאינון קָטְפִין בתר קדימתא וכ' (not קדמיתא) they cut the grapes after the first east wind after Succoth; a. fr.—Part. pass. קְטִיף. Koh. R. to XI, 9 כדון נחירך ק' וכ' now that thy nose is nipped (hanging down like a faded plant), thy ear heavy of hearing &c.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>קַטֵּיף</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition> same. Targ. Y. Lev. XXV, 11; a. e.—Lam. R. l. c., v. supra.—2) same.</definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to break off, interrupt</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ab. Zar. 72
<sup>b</sup> דקא מְקַטֵּיף קַטּוּפֵי (Rashi דמפסוקי פסוקי, read דמפסיק) he breaks off (the connection of the flow, withdraws the pouring vessel before the jet reaches the vessel into which the wine is poured). Ib. קַטְּפוּ קטופי (not קטפי; Ar. ed. Koh. קטיפתו) interrupt you the flow!</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Ithpe.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>אִתְקְטֵיף</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to be broken off, lopped, mutilated</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Is. XLVI, 1, sq. (h. text קרס). Targ. Jer. XLVIII, 25 (h. text נגדע); a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="S00812">
<head-word>קְטָף</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (preced.) [
<italic>incision</italic>,] 
<italic>resin gained by tapping, balsam</italic>; עץ הק' (or sub. עץ) 
<italic>balsam-tree</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Shebi. VII, 6 אין לק' וכ' the law of the Sabbatical year does not apply to the balsam tree; Tosef. ib. V, 12 יש לק' שביעית (ed. Zuck. לקט בש', corr. acc.) the law does apply; Y. Orl. I, 61
<sup>b</sup> bot. Nidd. 8
<sup>b</sup> קְטָפוֹ זה פריו its resin is its fruit. Ker. 6
<sup>a</sup> הצרי … מעצי ק' 
<italic>tsŏri</italic> is the sap that drips from resinous trees. Gen. R. s. 91, v. בַּלְסָם; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="S00873">

<head-word>קִדּ'</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (קָדַשׁ) </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>sanctification</italic>, esp. ק' השם the sanctification of the Name (of the Lord, v. 
<xref rid="S00123">קְדוּשָּׁה</xref>), 
<italic>loyalty to the Jewish faith, martyrdom</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Shebi. IV, 35
<sup>a</sup> bot. Pesik. B’shall., p. 87
<sup>a</sup>. Deut. R. s. 2 (ref. to Prov. XXIV, 21) אמר לו דבר של ק' שמי וכ' (not קידש שמא) the Lord said to Solomon, a thing which concerns the sanctification of my name (the unity of God) dost thou express by a brief allusion? Y. Kidd. IV, 65
<sup>c</sup> bot. גדול הוא ק' השם מחילול השם a positive act of sanctification of the Name is superior to (supersedes) a law which is to prevent profanation of the Name; בחילול השם כתיב … ובק' השם מתחלת וכ' concerning the profanation of the Name it is written (Deut. XXI, 23), ‘thou shalt not suffer his body to remain (even) over night &c.’, but when the Name was to be sanctified (by an act of retributive justice), it is written (II Sam. XXI, 10), ‘from the beginning of the harvest &c.’; Y. Snh. VI, 23
<sup>d</sup> (corr. acc.); a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. קִידּוּשִׁין</plural-form>
<italic>laws of sanctity</italic>. Y. Yeb. II, 3
<sup>d</sup> top למה סמך … לפרשת ק' why does the Biblical text join the chapter on sanctity (Lev. XIX) to that on incest (Lev. XVIII)?; (Lev. R. s. 24 לפרשת קְדוֹשִׁים, v. קָדוֹשׁ).</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>proclamation of sanctity; a</italic>) 
<italic>of the New Moon, seasons</italic> &c. (by the authorities).</definition>
<notes> Tosef. Snh. II, 1 ק' החדש ועיבור וכ' the proclamation of the New Moon and the intercalation of a month require a court of three. Y. ib. I, 18
<sup>c</sup> top חבירים … לק' הח' dare untitled scholars (v. חָבֵר) be admitted to sit on the proclamation of the New Moon?; a. fr.—B. Bath. 121
<sup>a</sup> מועדי יי' צריכין ק' בית דין וכ' the festivals of the Lord require to be regulated by the proclamation of the court, but the weekly Sabbath does not. Y. R. Hash. III, 58
<sup>d</sup> bot. ק' ב"ד the official proclamation of the jubilee; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. as ab. Ex. R. s. 15 קִדּוּשֵׁי החדשים</plural-form> the proceedings at the proclamation of the New Moon.—
<italic>b</italic>) 
<italic>proclamation of the sanctity of the day by special prayer, Ḳiddush</italic>. Pes. 100
<sup>a</sup> מפסיקין לק' when the Sabbath or Holy Day begins, we must interrupt a meal to recite Ḳiddush. Ib.
<sup>b</sup> ידי ק' יצאו they (that heard the Ḳiddush at synagogue) have complied with the duty of ushering the Sabbath in with Ḳiddush. Ib. 105
<sup>a</sup> sq. אם אין לו … ק' היום מפני שק' היום וכ' he who has only one cup of wine, recites over it the Ḳiddush of the day, because the sanctification of the day takes precedence of honoring the day (by grace after meal with wine). Meg. 27
<sup>b</sup> מכרה … והביאה לי ק' היום sold the bonnet on her head and procured for me the wine for the Ḳiddush of the day; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>washing hands and feet prior to a priestly function</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Zeb. 19
<sup>b</sup> כיצד מצות ק' how is the act of washing done? Ib. לינה מועלת ק' וכ' the intervention of the night has an effect on the sanctification of hands and feet, makes a renewed washing of hands and feet necessary. Ib. ק' שני the second sanctification (immediately before approaching the altar); Yoma 32
<sup>b</sup>; a. fr.—
<italic>Pl.</italic> as ab. Ib. III, 3. Ib. 32
<sup>b</sup>; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—4)</number>
<definition> (of mixed seeds) 
<italic>condemnation</italic> (v. 
<xref rid="S00191">קָדַשׁ</xref>
<italic>Pi.</italic> 7).</definition>
<notes> Yeb. 83
<sup>a</sup></notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—5)</number>
<definition>
<italic>putting ashes in the water of lustration; the ashes put in</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ib. 42
<sup>a</sup> bot. אסיפת אפרה … וק' (not לק', v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 50) the collecting of its ashes, the drawing of water and the putting in of the ashes; ib.
<sup>b</sup> Par. VI, 1 ונפל הק' וכ' and ashes fell on his hand. Ib. 2. Tosef. ib. VI (V), 1 עוסק עם הק' is engaged in the act of 
<italic>ḳiddush</italic>. Ib. 3 צריך ק' שני requires an additional putting in of ashes; a. fr.—
<italic>Pl.</italic> as ab. Ib. 5; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—6)</number>
<definition>
<italic>betrothal</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Mekh. Mishp. s. 3 ק' אחר ק' וכ' the father of a minor has the authority to give her away in marriage a second time &c., v. אַמְהוּת; אבל לא אמהות אחר ק' but he cannot hire her out after having once given her away. Y. Kidd. II, 62
<sup>c</sup> top נכללין בק' … בשלשה קידושין they (the three objects he gave her, when he said, ‘be betrothed with this, 
<italic>and</italic> this 
<italic>and</italic> this’) are combined to form one act of betrothal (which is valid, if the three objects combined have the legally prescribed value), and are separated (if he said, ‘be betrothed with this, with this, with this’) to form three acts of betrothal (and one of the objects at least must have the legal value); a. fr.—Pl. as ab. Ib.—Esp. 
<italic>ḳiddushin, the act of betrothal, legal and legitimate marriage</italic> (connubium). Kidd. IV, 9 קִידּוּשֶׁיהָ ק' her acceptance of the betrothal is a valid marriage; קִדּוּשָׁיו ק' his (the authorized messenger’s) acceptance is valid. Ib. III, 12 כל מקום שיש ק' ואין עברה וכ' wherever a betrothal is valid (where there is connubium), and no sin is connected with it, the issue follows the legal status of the male parent; וכל מקום שיש ק' ויש עברה וכ' but where the betrothal, if performed, is valid but sin is connected therewith, the issue has the status of the inferior parent, e. g. a widow married to a high priest. Ib. כל מי שאין לה עליו ק' אבל יש לה על אחרים ק' וכ' in a case where a marriage cannot take place with that special person (on account of consanguinity &c.), but may take place with others, the issue is a bastard (מַמְזֵר); וכל מי שאין לה לא עליו … ק' וכ' where a marriage cannot take place either with that special person or with other Israelites (she having no right of connubium), the issue follows the status of the mother. Yeb. 10
<sup>b</sup>, a. fr. אין ק' תופסין וכ' betrothal takes no effect in the case of &c. Kidd. 60
<sup>b</sup>, a. fr. קִידּוּשֵׁי ודאי an undisputed betrothal; קידושי ספק a legally doubtful betrothal; a. fr.—Trnsf. קִידּוּשִׁים, קִידּוּשִׁין, קִדּ' 
<italic>betrothal festivities</italic>, contrad. to wedding festivities. Num. R. s. 12 ועשה לה ק' גדולים and arranged for her sake large festivities; ib. (ref. to Ex. XX, 18) ולא היו אלא ק' and these were merely the solemnities of (Israel’s) betrothal (ref. to וקדשתם, ib. XIX, 10); Pesik. R. s. 5; Tanḥ. Naso 17.—
<italic>Ḳiddushin</italic>, name of a treatise of the Mishnah, Tosefta, Talmud Babli and Y’rushalmi, of the Order of Nashim. B. Bath. 52
<sup>b</sup> (a reference to Tosef. Kidd. I, 5) תני רב … בק' דבי לוי Rab … taught from the treatise of Ḳiddushin of the school of Levi (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 1).</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="S00880">
<head-word>קִיּוּהָא</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (קְהֵי) [
<italic>that which blunts or loosens the teeth</italic>,] 
<italic>acid, acrid taste</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Pes. 74
<sup>b</sup> sq. התם איתא לק' … ליתיה לק' וכ' there (in the case of stale vinegar) the acid of the fruit is present (in its natural condition), here (in vinegar which has once been used for drawing the blood from meat) the acid is no longer pure. Keth. 61
<sup>a</sup> כל … ואית ליה ק' any food that has a penetrating savor or an acrid taste (is injurious to him in whose presence it is partaken of without his being permitted a taste of it). Ib. 75
<sup>a</sup> ק' דחמרא (Ar. s. v. משק: מקוה) wine that has turned sour. Midr. Till. to Ps. LXXV, 9 יכול ק' lest you think, sour (stale) wine is meant; (Yalk. ib. 813 דוחה, v. דָּהָה).</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="S00881">
<head-word>קִיוּוּי</head-word>

<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (קָוָה) 
<italic>hope, faith</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 98 הכל בק' יסורין בק' וכ' in every condition of life faith is a potent factor, sufferings are borne by faith, sanctification of the Name (martyrdom) rests on faith &c. Yalk. Ps. 736 (ref. to Ps. XL, 2) אם אין ביד ישראל אלא הק' כדאי הן לגאולה בשכר הק' if Israel possess no merit except faith, it is worthy of redemption as a reward for its faith; Midr. Till. to Ps. l. c. (corr. acc.). Yalk. Ex. 241 (ref. to Ps. l. c.) מתוך הק' ויט אלי וכ' out of this hope it came to pass that he inclined to me &c.; Tanḥ. ed. Bub., B’shall. 12; ib. (ref. to Ps. XXVII, 14) אם בא קִוּוּיְךָ יפה וכ' (not קויך) if what thou hast hoped for, comes to pass, it is well; if not, hope again; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="S00884">
<head-word>קִיּוּם</head-word>
<head-word>קִיּיוּם</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (קוּם) </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>preservation; storage.</italic></definition>
<notes> Peah I, 4 ומכניסו לק' and what one brings in for storage (not for immediate use); Y. ib. I, 16
<sup>c</sup> top. Ib. bot. דבר שאינו לק' a thing which is not intended or fit for storage. Y. Sabb. VII, 9
<sup>a</sup> top; Bab. ib. 68
<sup>a</sup>. Ab. Zar. 74
<sup>b</sup> זה מכניסו לק' וכ' Ms. M. (ed. בק') the one (vessel) one brings in for storage (to leave the wine there for some time) &c., v. מוּכְנָס. Y. Kil. II, 27
<sup>d</sup> bot. מקומו … שאינו רוצה בקִיּוּמוֹ the place where it grows is evidence that he does not want its preservation (to cultivate it). Yoma 45
<sup>a</sup> אחת של ק' האש one pile for the purpose of keeping up the fire; Tosef. ib. III (II), 23 אחת לק' האש (ed. Zuck. לקיים, corr. acc.); Y. ib. IV, 41
<sup>d</sup> bot. מערכת קִיּוּמֵי אש (pl.); a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>basis, foundation</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Kil. IX, 32
<sup>a</sup> (in Chald. dict.) אילין פליגין על דרב ולית להון ק' (not דבר) these opinions conflict with Rab’s, and have no foundation; Y. Hag. II, end, 78
<sup>c</sup></notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition> (law) 
<italic>substantiation, attestation, identification</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gitt. 3
<sup>a</sup> ק' שטרות the identification of signatures on documents (certification before court). Y. ib. II, beg. 44
<sup>a</sup> כלום קִיּוּמוֹ של גט וכ' is there any other way of authenticating a letter of divorce than through the declarations of its signers? Gen. R. s. 78 (ref. to Esau’s declaration, Gen. XXXIII, 9) אין ק' חגט וכ' there is no better attestation to the legality of a document than through its signers. B. Mets. 21
<sup>a</sup> עדי ק' signature of witnesses to the authentication before court. B. Bath. X, 6 ועושין לו ק' איש וכ' and the court makes out a certificate, This man’s document was effaced &c.; Tosef. ib. XI, 8, sq.; Y. ib. X, 17
<sup>c</sup> bot.; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<number>1)</number>
<definition> = לְקִיחָה, 
<italic>taking, acquiring</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Yeb. 97
<sup>a</sup> (ref. to Lev. XX, 11-14) בכולן נאמר שכיבה וכאן נאמר ק' וכ' with reference to all of them the word ‘sleeping’ is used, but here (v. 14) ‘taking’ is used, to intimate that the law punishes the marriage only (and not the sexual connection out of wedlock). Ib. הכי נמי הנך ק' הוא וכ' do you really say with reference to these (v. 17) that the law forbids only marriage? (Answer) ליקוחין … הראוי לק' ק' וכ' the verb 
<italic>laḳaḥ</italic> is used as a general term: where a regular marriage might have taken place (under other circumstances), the text prohibits marriage; where only sexual connection can be meant, the verb 
<italic>laḳaḥ</italic> has the meaning of 
<italic>shakhab</italic>. Kidd. 2
<sup>a</sup>, a. e. גמר ק' ק' וכ' we learn the mode of acquiring (לקח in Deut. XXII, 13) from the acquisition of the field of Ephron (Gen. XXIII, 13 קח); Ḥull. 82
<sup>a</sup>; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. קִיחוֹת</plural-form>. Yoma 3
<sup>b</sup> בק' דעלמא וכ' in general cases where the text uses קח, …, but here (Ex. XXX, 23) it says expressly קח לך (take unto thee, at thy own expense).</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>

<italic>handle</italic>,]

XVI, 4 התורמל</plural-form> … קִיחוֹתָיו (Ar. קיה', Var. קיח') the shepherd’s bag is susceptible of uncleanness, when one has made the rim, trimmed it, and attached the thongs with which to tie it up. <entry id="S00999">

<italic>it is</italic>) 
<italic>established, certain</italic>; ק' ל־ 
<italic>to be certain, to know</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Sabb. 136
<sup>a</sup> ק' לי ביה וכ' I am certain that its (the infant’s) months were complete (that it was no abortion). Ab. Zar. 76
<sup>b</sup> מר ק' לי בגוויה וכ' I am sure about this gentleman (that he is a strict observer); about you I am not. Kidd. 66

<italic>he who has committed two offences simultaneously, must be held answerable for the severer only</italic>. Gitt. 52
<sup>b</sup> מנסך קם ליה בדר' מ' he who uses his neighbor’s wine for idolatrous libation (and makes the remainder unavailabe), is exempt from making restitution for the wine, because he has to suffer the severer penalty, which is death. Ib. 53
<sup>a</sup> משום דלא ק' ל' בדר' מ' because this is no case of a severer penalty (when he makes his neighbor’s wine unclean). Ḥull. 81
<sup>b</sup> קם ל' בדר' מ' (Ms. M. קָאִים) he suffers the severer penalty (for slaughtering for idolatrous purposes, and is exempt from the penalty of stripes for slaughtering the dam and her child in one day); a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>
